deep.reconstruction:
Setting, continued from p.4. M is a category equipped with a class M_as of 'aspheric objects', and i: A → M is a functor from a small category. It induces i*: M → A^, x ↦ Hom_M(i(-), x). Call i 'M_as-aspheric' if i*(x) is aspheric in A^ for every x in M_as. Page 4 asked whether this forces i* to be conservative and faithful. It recalled the presheaf case: for an aspheric functor f: A → B, f*: B^ → A^ is conservative and faithful, because every A/b is aspheric, hence nonempty, so f is 'dominant'. It concluded that for i* to be faithful one needs M → M_as^ to be faithful, i.e. M_as must be generating. It also began testing degenerate cases (M_as empty, M_as a single object).

This page, first block: the degenerate test case. Take A with a single object a and put G = End(a), so A^ ≃ G-sets. Suppose G = {id_a}. Then A^ ≃ (Ens), and the aspheric sets are the one-point sets. Hence the aspheric objects of M for which i is aspheric are M_as = {x ∈ Ob M | Hom(a,x) has cardinal 1}. Proposed counterexample: M a discrete category of cardinal ≥ 2 (so M_as = {a}). Grothendieck then decides to add the hypothesis that M_as generates M, in the sense that M → M_as^ is faithful and conservative.

Second block (struck through with long diagonal strokes, i.e. abandoned or provisional): functoriality between two such 'asphericity structures' M and M'. Take f*: M' → M commuting with projective limits. A left adjoint f_! exists if limit-preserving functors on M' are (co)representable. This can be ensured by accessibility hypotheses on f*, i.e. an adjoint functor theorem. He then asks whether one should require f_! to send M_as into M'_as. As a test he asks: if f: A → B is aspheric, is f_!(A^_as) ⊂ B^_as? He starts the case B = point, A aspheric, and the page ends.

That test case works: f_! = colim = π_0, and an aspheric presheaf X has connected A/X, so π_0(X) = point, which is aspheric in (Ens). In general, (f_!X)(b) = colim over the comma category b\A of X, so f_! is governed by the categories b\A. Asphericity of f is a condition on the categories A/b instead. This variance mismatch suggests the inclusion fails in general, and that the natural condition is rather on b\A ('co-asphericity'). The whole page belongs to the 1983 development of 'asphericity structures' on modelizers, test functors with values in a modelizer, and morphisms between them, which is the material of Pursuing Stacks.
errors: The counterexample 'M discrete of cardinal ≥ 2' is not a counterexample in the usual sense. In a discrete category every functor out of M is trivially faithful and conservative, so i* = Hom(a,-): M → Ens is both. What fails is the stronger presheaf-style criterion borrowed from p.4: i*(x) = ∅ ⇒ x initial, i.e. M_as = {a} does not separate or generate the objects of M (all x ≠ a go to ∅). Grothendieck's conclusion, to impose that M_as generate M, is the right fix, but the stated failure needs this stronger notion or extra structure on M (e.g. finite limits or an initial object).

Minor: 'foncteurs sur M' qui commutent aux lim ← sont représentables' should read corepresentable (covariant functors M' → Ens). This is the usual adjoint-functor-theorem formulation, with a solution-set or accessibility condition required, as he himself notes.

The final question (does f_! preserve aspheric presheaves for aspheric f?) is left open. It holds for B = point, but in general f_! is computed with the comma categories b\A, not A/b, so asphericity of f does not obviously control it. A general positive answer should not be expected without extra hypotheses.

ideas.what: Single-object test case: A^ ≃ G-sets; for trivial G, aspheric objects of Ens are the singletons, so the induced M_as is {x | Hom(a,x) is a singleton}.
ideas.modern_name: asphericity of sets / discrete categories (a discrete category is weakly contractible iff it is a point)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; Grothendieck's asphericity framework (Pursuing Stacks), systematized by Maltsiniotis (Astérisque 301, 2005)
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks treats asphericity structures in detail; this exact test case: unsure

ideas.what: Requiring that the aspheric objects M_as generate M, so that M → M_as^ is faithful and conservative.
ideas.modern_name: generating (dense or separating) family of aspheric objects in an asphericity structure

ideas.what: Existence of f_! left adjoint to a limit-preserving f*: M' → M under representability or accessibility hypotheses.
ideas.where_published: SGA 4 Exp. I (representability and adjoint criteria); used informally in Pursuing Stacks

ideas.what: Question whether for aspheric f: A → B the left Kan extension f_!: A^ → B^ sends aspheric presheaves to aspheric presheaves, as a model for 'morphisms of asphericity structures'.
ideas.modern_name: preservation of weakly contractible presheaves by u_!; compatibility of morphisms of asphericity structures / test functors
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Pursuing Stacks); Maltsiniotis, Cisinski (Astérisque 308) for homotopical properties of u_!
ideas.where_published: related discussions of i_! and test functors in Pursuing Stacks; this precise question: unsure

missed.claim: Grothendieck asks whether f_! preserves aspheric objects for an aspheric functor f: A → B, checks only the start of the case B = point, and stops. The asphericity of f concerns A/b, while f_! is computed over b\A, so the natural sufficient condition is on the b\A side. The page leaves this mismatch implicit.
missed.quote: Si f: A → B asphérique, a-t-on f_!(A^_as) ⊂ B^_as ? Par exemple, prenons B ponctuelle, A cat. asph.,
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is essentially known territory: Maltsiniotis and Cisinski treat when u_! preserves weak equivalences or aspheric objects. It is mainly of historical interest as showing how the axioms for morphisms of asphericity structures were tested. Not new.

deep.surprise_reason: Working scratch notes from the 1983 asphericity-structure material that became part of Pursuing Stacks. The page contains a degenerate test case, the decision to require M_as to be generating, and an adjoint-functor existence remark. The only open thread (f_! preserving aspheric presheaves) is abandoned and is covered by later work of Maltsiniotis and Cisinski.
transcription_corrections: 'End(6)', '{1d_6}', 'Hom(6, x)': the symbol is almost certainly the object 'a', so read G = End(a), G = {id_a}, Hom(a, x).
'On ne suppose que M_as engendre M' → most likely 'On va supposer que M_as engendre M' (the hypothesis is being imposed).
'qu'il faut[?] pas[?] : faire des hyp. d'accessibilité sur f*' → plausibly 'quitte peut-être à faire des hyp. d'accessibilité sur f*'.
'Mais voulons ... supposer que f_! envoie[?] M_as dans M'_as ?' → 'Mais voulons-nous supposer que f_! envoie M_as dans M'_as ?'
The whole lower half (from the M ← M' diagram down to the end) is struck through by long diagonal strokes; the crossed-out 'A ⇄' at the left of the first diagram is also cancelled.
'Si f: A → B asphérique, a-t-on' (the transcription's 'a-t-on' is correct; 'asphérique' is abbreviated in the image).
